verdict.rationale: Penpot's own docs say it outputs code from designs: an inspect mode that yields CSS, HTML, SVG and JSON, plus CSS Grid/Flex layouts so the markup reflects real layout rules. The GitHub README adds that design is 'expressed as code, enabling a direct translation'. However, nothing shows component-to-code mappings into a codebase, or that the generated code is production-ready rather than reference snippets. Missing for 10: documented component-to-code mapping to real code components, evidence the generated HTML/CSS is shippable as-is, and independent or hands-on corroboration of output quality.

support.subject: As a developer, designs map to production code — component-to-code mappings or direct design-to-code output I can actually ship

citations.quote: Inspect and integrate code that actually matches design. Enjoy open standards like CSS, HTML, SVG and JSON as well as Penpot's open file format.
design is expressed as code, enabling a direct translation and shipping products faster.
Design responsive and rules-based interfaces with wireframes, interactive prototypes, and CSS Grid and Flex layouts.
